content: Imagine you are playing outside. Suddenly, you feel a tiny prick on your arm. A mosquito! A few days later, you are shivering under blankets with a high fever. How did a creature smaller than a peanut defeat you?
Do you think mosquitoes carry poison, or do they put something else inside our body when they bite us?

content.title: The Tiny Syringe
content.description: When a female Anopheles mosquito bites, she doesn't just suck your blood. She injects tiny invisible germs called 'Plasmodium' into your bloodstream, like a doctor giving an injection!

content: These germs multiply in our blood, causing a dangerous disease. We can only find these germs by looking at a drop of blood under a microscope!

content.definition: A serious disease caused by a parasite, transmitted by the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes, characterized by severe chills and high fever.

question: What does a female Anopheles mosquito inject into our body that causes Malaria?

content: Have you ever seen a poster warning about Malaria? Why do they always tell us to clean our water coolers and not let water collect in old tires? Explain it to your younger sibling.

Blood tests aren't just for finding Malaria. When Aarti felt very weak, her blood test didn't show germs. It showed she had less 'Haemoglobin' (iron) in her blood. This is called Anaemia! It connects to what we eat.

content.definition: A condition in which there is a deficiency of red cells or of haemoglobin in the blood, resulting in pallor and weariness.

content: To prevent Anaemia, we must eat iron-rich foods like jaggery (gur), amla, and green leafy vegetables. Food is our best medicine!

People often think that spraying chemicals is the only way to stop mosquitoes. The easiest way is to put fish in ponds! The fish eat the mosquito larvae (baby mosquitoes) before they can even grow wings.

question: Which of the following is the most natural way to stop mosquitoes from breeding in ponds?
options: Putting fish in the pond to eat mosquito larvae

content: Your mission today: Check your home for stagnant water. Empty any pots, coolers, or tires. Become a Mosquito Hunter!
